name: Extend workforce identity continuity to payroll and sensitive lifecycle events

attribution.legal_posture: First-party Socure product and guidance statements support a defensive lifecycle control. Incident disclosure, product endorsement, measured effectiveness, legal identity, nationality, and DPRK attribution fall outside the statements.

caveats: A payroll, direct-deposit, credential, benefits, or access change triggers review; fraud or DPRK affiliation requires corroborating evidence.
Apply lawful purpose, data minimization, bounded retention, security, accessibility, consistent treatment, trained human review, correction, and appeal.
DPRK affiliation requires more than nationality, accent, language, appearance, disability, geography, remote-work status, payment method, camera behavior, or any single inconsistency.

Email age, phone-name correlation, device/network context, location consistency, document review, liveness, professional-profile history, and payment-change events are review signals for closer review. DPRK affiliation and fraud findings require cited sources; apply controls lawfully, proportionately, consistently, with human review and appeal paths.
This record retains no person, persona, account, organization, image, identity document, biometric artifact, credential, financial selector, device or network selector or private applicant data.
Publish this as a defensive lifecycle control; it is not a product endorsement, and any payroll or account change receives case-specific review.
Suspected or vendor-assessed linkage is an unconfirmed attribution; legal identity, adjudication, and harm require separate evidence.
Use renewed verification only for defined identity-sensitive events and documented risk; avoid indiscriminate continuous surveillance.

infrastructure.statement: Socure describes workforce identity review as a lifecycle control spanning application, interview, onboarding, and employment rather than a one-time background check. The material incremental control is risk-based renewed verification at payroll setup, direct-deposit changes, password resets, benefits changes, and sensitive-access changes, with lower-friction handling for lower-risk cases and trained human review for escalations.
infrastructure.evidence_class: provider-described defensive control model; source provenance and described design are confirmed, but product efficacy is not independently validated

sources.support: Socure says its recruiters found several fabricated applicants. It describes one applicant that it assessed as likely tied to a North Korean employment-fraud scam; the applicant did not complete requested document and live-selfie verification or attend the follow-up interview. Provenance: The visible page and JSON-LD both provide the 2025-05-29 publication date; JSON-LD provides the 2025-10-16 modification date. The page is the claim-bearing first-party source. A Fortune article linked by Socure is corroborating reporting, not the basis for Socure's own observations
sources.locator: Opening through 'Socure vs. Fake Job Applicants'; applicant-pool measurements; applicant comparison; follow-up verification; 'What Employers Should Do'

sources.support: Socure defines workforce verification as continuous from application through employment. It identifies onboarding, payroll setup, direct-deposit changes, password resets, benefits enrollment, and sensitive-access changes as identity-sensitive moments and recommends risk-based step-up review rather than equal friction for every applicant. Provenance: The visible page and JSON-LD provide the 2026-06-05 publication date; JSON-LD provides the 2026-06-10 modification date. DPRK scale statistics on this page are attributed to third-party reporting and were not retained as first-party evidence
sources.locator: 'What is workforce verification?'; lifecycle stages; 'At payroll and beyond'; risk-based verification; FAQ

sources.support: Socure says its solution integrates with HR platforms, job boards, payroll systems, and applicant-tracking systems. It describes identity-risk review at application and ongoing assessment through recruiting, hiring, and onboarding, and it restates the probabilistic assessment of the same applicant encounter. Provenance: The release has a visible July 16, 2025 dateline and embeds the complete claim-bearing text in first-party page data
sources.locator: Dateline and opening; integration and risk-monitoring paragraphs; Rivka Gewirtz Little quotation; DPRK context paragraph
